title: Operational priming fidelity safelist and sanity catalog
author: Sofia Patel
summary: A compact, operational reference that defines allowed priming patterns (the 'priming safelist'), a categorized catalog of lightweight sanity probes to run during onboarding and rollout, and concrete monitoring thresholds for detecting priming-induced fidelity regressions across quantized and cached serving environments.
body:
Summary

Purpose: This document codifies a repeatable operational approach to validate that prompt priming (templates, system messages, and few-shot exemplars) does not introduce brittle behavior when models are deployed across mixed-precision, KV-cached, and prefix-cached runtime variants. It provides: a priming safelist (allowed patterns and constraints), a catalog of sanity probes grouped by failure mode, an onboarding checklist for model/prompts, and measurable alert thresholds for automated triage.

Scope
- Applies to: model onboarding for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments; eval harness shadow runs; and rapid canary rollouts that include mixed-precision or KV-cache fallbacks.
- Excludes: deep safety content audits (see safety-sandbox) and longtail human-in-the-loop annotation processes.

Key definitions
- Priming: any fixed text injected into context prior to user input (system prompts, instructions, exemplars).
- Priming-induced drift: reproducible change in task fidelity attributable to priming text interacting with model variant (quantized kernels, sequence-length changes, cache shards).
- Sanity probe: a small, deterministic or semi-deterministic example used to detect regressions early in rollout.

Motivation
Priming patterns that pass on a full-precision baseline can fail subtly when a model is quantized or served from a warmed KV cache. Failures range from hallucination rate increases on factual probes to function-call argument corruption and response truncation. Operational teams need a compact, automatable checklist and a short suite of probes that run quickly during shadow or micro-canary stages to avoid noisy rollouts.

Priming safelist (operational constraints)
1) System-message length: prefer <= 480 tokens for long-context models; hard-fail > 1024 tokens in any onboarding evaluation. Rationale: kernel dispatch decisions and cache priming penalties increase with system length.
2) Exemplars: at most 3 exemplars per prompt for interactive routes; prefer single-turn compact examples (max 60 tokens each).
3) Structured instructions: when emitting JSON or function calls, include an explicit schema line (e.g., "Return a single JSON object matching schema:...") as the final priming line to anchor tokenization.
4) Temperature-sensitive segments: avoid mixing high-entropy creative instructions inside the same priming block used for deterministic extraction tasks.
5) Token budget anchors: reserve at least 20% of average route token budget for model output during micro-canary runs to detect truncation.
6) Disallowed patterns: do not use dynamic time/date placeholders in priming text that mutate between shadow and prod runs (these create false positives).

Sanity catalog (fast probes to include in automation)
Group A — Deterministic fidelity probes (run first; <500ms baseline runtime)
- Short factual QA (3 seeds): expect >= 95% canonical-answer match on baseline model.
- JSON-schema emission (4 seeds): exact-match on keys and types for all seeds.

Group B — Interaction/ordering probes (detect cache/priming order sensitivity)
- Reordering sensitivity (5 seeds): prompt set where ordering of exemplars should not change discrete classification output.
- Prefix collision probe: verify that inserted priming suffixes don't collide with tokenized user anchors.

Group C — Quantization stress probes (detect precision-induced drift)
- Numeric stability (6 seeds): arithmetic or numeric comparator tasks that historically regress under 4-bit quantization. Threshold: median absolute error increase <= 0.02 vs baseline.
- Function-call argument integrity (3 seeds): ensure argument strings and types survive a quantized variant.

Group D — Latency & truncation probes (detect runtime truncation/fallbacks)
- Long-output continuity (2 seeds): expected output length >= 80% of baseline; flag if < 80%.
- Streaming boundary check: confirm partial-incremental tokens don't produce malformed JSON at stream boundaries.

Categorized probe metadata (what to store in the eval manifest)
- probe_id (string), intent (classification/generation/json/functioncall), seeds (integer), expected_assertion (string), severity (low/medium/high), run_time_budget_ms (integer).

Onboarding checklist (minimal, numbered steps to include in the model promotion pipeline)
1) Baseline capture: run Group A+B probes against baseline full-precision shadow and store golden outputs (eval-asset-registry).
2) Mixed-variant shadow runs: run the entire Sanity Catalog against 1) quantized candidate, 2) candidate with prefix-caching enabled, 3) candidate with KV-cache warmed for common tenants. Collect diffs.
3) Delta scoring: compute the three primary deltas: fidelity (accuracy/JSON-key-match), numeric drift (MAE), and structural integrity (functioncall key mismatches).
4) Priming safelist verification: automated linting of priming text against the six safelist constraints; generate lint findings.
5) Micro-canary: deploy to 1% traffic with shadow telemetry enabled (collect probe pass rates and resource metrics for 24–72 hours).
6) Gate decision: pass to rollout if: Group A pass rate >= 98%, Group B pass rate >= 95%, no Group C probe exceeding severity=high.

Rollout & fallback policy (practical knobs)
- Canary duration: default 48h with minimum 2000 routed inference calls or 2,000 probe samples, whichever comes first.
- Auto-fallback triggers (automatic rollback to baseline variant):
  - Any Group A probe regression > 3 standard deviations over baseline for two consecutive windows (15m each).
  - Any Group C numeric drift median > 0.05 (MAE) or functioncall structural failure rate > 1%.
  - Streaming/truncation alerts: if > 0.5% of long-output probes return below 60% length for two consecutive hours.

Monitoring & alert thresholds (concrete values)
- Probe pass-rate SLO: 99.5% (monthly) for Group A on production-critical routes.
- Short-term alert: probe pass-rate drop > 1.0 percentage point within 30 minutes triggers P1 review.
- Numeric drift threshold: MAE increase > 0.03 triggers P2.
- Functioncall schema mismatch rate > 0.5% triggers P1 escalation.

Automated triage playbook (quick steps for oncall)
1) Confirm alert: open the associated probe run artifacts in eval-mesh and capture the diff heatmap.
2) Check rollout stage: if canary, pause traffic and expand shadow sampling to increase probe density.
3) Isolate vector: toggle quantization fallback to baseline (one click rollback) and re-run failing probes; if failures stop, tag as quant-fidelity.
4) If toggling cache solves the issue, document cache-priming keys and apply prefix-shrink mitigation.
5) If unresolved, escalate to applied-ml oncall with artifacts and hypothesis matrix.

Ownership and communication
- Primary owner: Applied ML - Model Quality (team: applied-ml-quality).
- Secondary owner: Serving Runtime (team: eng-serving-runtime) for kernel/quant issues.
- Communications: any P1 must generate a one-paragraph status on the public incident channel and a retrospective doc within 7 days.

Example quick commands and config snippets
- Run the priming safelist linter locally:
  ri-eval lint-priming --file my_template.txt --ruleset safelist-2026
- Run the compact sanity catalog against a candidate model (shadow):
  ri-eval run --catalog sanity-catalog-compact --model candidate-v2 --variant quant-4bit --output artifacts/candidate-v2/sanity.json --parallel 8

Example probe manifest entry (store as a one-line JSON in the eval-asset-registry):
  {"probe_id":"priming_json_schema_01","intent":"json","seeds":4,"expected_assertion":"keys: [id,items,total]","severity":"high","run_time_budget_ms":1200}

Best practices and mitigations (operational recommendations)
- Keep priming texts compact and descriptive; prefer a single final anchoring sentence that defines output format.
- When migrating to a quantized runtime, run numeric-stability probes with increased seed diversity to reduce variance.
- Maintain a small stable set of Group A probes mapped to each customer-critical route — these provide the earliest warning for regressions.

Related pages
- ../eval-harness/latency-sensitivity-eval-routing-fallback-protocol-2026.json
- ../model-onboarding/onboarding-fidelity-sla-and-noise-budget-manifest-2026.json

Appendix: common failure signatures and suggested remediations
- Hallucination spike paired with prefix-caching: shrink system prompt or whitelist caching for the route.
- Functioncall key truncation under streaming: add explicit trailing bracket anchors in priming.
